name: Abu Cemetery
desc_parts: Location needs to be confirmed.

This small cemetery has five graves surrounded by a fence of thorny bushes. It needs a gate for easy access. At the time of this writing there was only one remaining Bene Israel family taking care of this cemetery.

name: Agarwada Cemetery
desc_parts: This small cemetery has only 5 graves which are unprotected. But in spite of that the graves are intact and well kept with 2 graves being newly rebuilt. Domestic animals freely graze at this site without any hindrance.

name: Ahmedabad New Cemetery
desc_parts: The land for Ahmedabad's new cemetery was donated by the Best family.

name: Ahmedabad Old Cemetery
desc_parts: Location needs to be verified.

The old cemetery has about 300 graves all are well looked after at time of writing by Mr. Joseph Pingle the Hazan of the synagogue. The cemetery is protected by a wall surrounding the area with an iron gate as well as guards.

name: Ambepur Cemetery
desc_parts: The cemetery here is not protected. Most of the graves are destroyed and the few remaining have a bleek outlook.
There is also a synagogue here too and its premises are protected.

name: Ashtami Cemetery
desc_parts: At this cemetery the author identified 17 graves 14 of which belonged to the Ashtamkar family. There were burials until 1997 when the last Bene Israel family finally left to Israel. There was also a synagogue in Ashtami. The graves are in an open space without any fence around them.

name: Ashtoba Sidheshwar Cemetery
desc_parts: Location of the marker needs to be verified.

All the graves in this small cemetery belong to the Varsulkar family. The latest being from 1996 and earliest from 1877. There are no Bene Israel families living around this area. Therefore no one is taking care of this cemetery. At the time of writing the author notes that local farmers are encroaching on this area but disputes among themselves have kept them at bay so far. The cemetery is also in danger of being washed away due to its proximity to a fast flowing river.

name: Awas Cemetery
desc_parts: There are two cemeteries in Awas. The old one near Rane Ali and the new one near ESCO Paltry. In the old cemetery there are no headstones

name: Bandra Bene Israel Cemetery
desc_parts: Bandra cemetery has about 60 graves. It is well kept but needs renovation. It was opened on December 23 1945.

name: Bankundi Jewish Cemetery (Borli)
desc_parts: This cemetery is almost destroyed. Villagers have destroyed most of the graves while digging the earth around for building purposes. The earliest intact grave identified by the author was of the late Yoseph Solomon Sankar from 1842. There are no signs leading to this cemetery. Anybody can enter this cemetery. There are two Bene Israel families living here and there's a synagogue here as well (but no community prayers are conducted).

name: Bhatsai
desc_parts: This is not really a cemetery but only a single grave. It is located at the enterance to the village.

name: Cheul Cemetery
desc_parts: There are approximately 150 graves at this cemetery and about 63 are in good condition. Most of the graves were washed out by rain.

People from nearby villages of Revdanda and Warsoli also buried their dead here. There are 2 graves here where you will find two and three names on the headstone. The grave itself is also divided into two and three parts.
Kehimkar mentions in his book that a person by the name Rahabi may have visited Cheul and helped revive Judaism among the Bene Israel.

name: Chinchpokli Baghdadi Cemetery
desc_parts: Location approximated.
This cemetery is exclusively reserved for the burial of Baghdadi Jews. This cemetery is in a very good condition and the expenses for this cemetery are borne by the Sassoon Cemetery Fund.
There are about 250 graves at this cemetery. The author adds that there has been a record of approximately 1 000 graves at this cemetery.

name: Chorde Cemetery
desc_parts: This is a small cemetery with only 5 graves. There are no Bene Israel living in this village. The cemetery is unguarded and untended.

name: Delhi Cemetery
desc_parts: There are about 150 graves at this cemetery. There is a caretaker to attend to the cleanliness of the cemetery. The oldest grave here is from 1934.
The below grave belongs to a German from Bonn by the name Herbert Apfel (?)

name: Disa Cemetery
desc_parts: Disa Cemetery is completely destroyed. Around 2003 there were still 3 graves of the Dighorkar family. By 2005 they were destroyed and only rubble stood at this place.

name: Galsur Cemetery
desc_parts: This is a small cemetery with only 4 graves. All the graves belong to the Mapgavkar family. They are all about 50-60 years old. There is nothing to protect these graves which are not in good condition.

name: Gondhalpada Cemetery
desc_parts: This is a large and active cemetery. Recently departed Individuals from Alibag Varsoli and Pali are brought here for burial. This cemetery has no fence to protect it. Domestic animals graze freely here and damage the graves. Many headstones have fallen down and embedded into the ground. There's no one to perform maintenance work at this cemetery. Wild growth is found around many of the graves and it is not easy to approach all the existing graves.
The author identified 54 graves and the earliest is from 1834. There is an active synagogue in Alibag.

name: Grant Road
desc_parts: Location needs to be verified.
This cemetery is now a municipal dumping ground. This cemetery was opened on January 30 1874. Over 2 decades ago it used to have approximately 100 graves.

name: Igatpuri Cemetery
desc_parts: There are about 20 graves at this cemetery near the flour mill. Most of the graves belong to Umardekar family. At one point this cemetery was used as a drinking and drug hangout by some delinquent youth.

In 2000 Mr. Joseph Daniel Belkar and Mr. Eliezer Umardekar decided to get a stone wall built around this cemetery. In spite of threats from these delinquent youths these men got the job completed with the help of the local police. This wall was built at the personal cost of 65 000 rupees.
The oldest grave in this cemetery is from 1903.

name: Jabalpur Cemetery
desc_parts: This cemetery is far away from the main city. There is a wall around this cemetery and the gate is locked. There are hutments around the cemetery wall and a lot of waste dumped at the cemetery gate. A plaque outside the gate indicates it is a Bene israel cemetery.

There are 24 graves at this cemetery and most of them are well maintained. The existing families are planning to settle in Mumbai. Therefore there will be no one left behind to look after this cemetery.

name: Jambhulpada Cemetery
desc_parts: There's a small cemetery right outside the village. It is in an open field containing 5 graves of the Varsulkar family. The oldest grave is from 1743 of Rebbecabai Varulkar. This is 33 years before the United States Declaration of Independence was wirtten on July 4

name: Kolkata Jewish Cemetery
desc_parts: Baghdadi cemetery

name: Kurul Cemetery
desc_parts: This long forgotten cemetery is situated near a marshy land in Kurul. The author observed several headstones embedded deeply into the ground. These headstones could not be reached due to hazardous conditions. The author did manage to find 2 graves that were accessible. He notes one of Milkabai (died in 1829) and the other of Sakoji Abrahamji Cheulkar (died in 1841).

name: Mazgaon Cemetery
desc_parts: At this cemetery both Bene Israels and Baghdadi Jews were buried side-by-side. This cemetery was closed to burial on January 8

name: Murud Cemetery
desc_parts: Eleven graves are found at this cemetery. A wire fence is built around this cemetery with community funds. Part of the fence and gate were pulled down by the Neo Buddhists. They claimed that some of the land did not belong to the Jewish cemetery. The gate and fence were fixed to exclude the area clamied by the Neo Buddhists.

name: Nagpada
desc_parts: This cemetery at Nagpada was opened in 1785. Today a municipal garden stands at this site with only 1 grave. Bene Israel graves of 1817-1821 were found here. 45 Bene Israel community members were buried here according to a book by David Sassoon "Ohel David".
The one existing grave belongs to Mr. Sillamon Nussim Rajpurkar Cajee. He passed away on July 20 1828 (age 45)

name: Nandgaon Cemetery
desc_parts: Verify marker location.
The graves here are very unique. The older graves have inscriptions in Marathi and the later ones have also Hebrew names and dates.
Cheulkar family of Nandgav is looking after 20 odd graves here. This cemetery is unfenced.

name: Navgav Cemetery
desc_parts: Navgav cemetery is supposedly over 2000 years old. According to tradition the ancestors of the Bene Israels were shipwrecked off the coast of Konkan. A monument is built at this site.

There are 26 unharmed graves at this cemetery. Additional graves have only stones around them to serve as markers. In the past wooden markers were used to identify a grave. The author was told by the cemetery keeper that a previous keeper has sold all those wooden markers for firewood and therefore was removed from this post.
During the author's visit he noted that only half of the wall surrounding this cemetery is complete. No signs of work to complete the wall were seen.
The photograph below say that the grave belongs to Shmuel Benjamin Naogawkar passed away on Friday May 1778.
The photograph below shows a headstones belonging to the grave of Moshe Ben Yosef Belkar passed away away in 1748.

name: Palanpur Cemetery
desc_parts: Palanpur cemetery is walled within the confines of the Christian cemetery. Only one Bene Israel family has a key to its gate. No more burials are conducted here.

name: Pali Cemetery
desc_parts: At one time about 25 Bene Israel families used to live here. A synagogue is also in the vicinity. But today only the Hazan prays at the synagogue and there is no Minyan.

The cemetery has about 24 graves with headstones. The author was told by a local woman that the Pali municipality has recognized that the cemetery needs protection. A separate road is to be built leading to the cemetery as well as a fence.
The oldest grave identified by the author was from 1769.

name: Panvel Cemetery
desc_parts: Panvel cemetery is in a dilapidated and neglected condition. Hutments were built around and on some graves. Some graves were within the boundries of these homes. The author also observed tarred clothes hanging off the graves. Hutments dwellers blocked access to some graves as they stored their belonging there. Several graves were in good condition. Those were located around the center of the cemetery.

The author remarked that when the Sifrei Torah were damaged during the floods in 2005 they were buried at the Worli cemetery. Commenting that it was probably not "worthwhile to bury their Sefer Torahs in this uncared for cemetery".

name: Pen Bene Israel Cemetery
desc_parts: The Pen cemetery has ancient graved dating back to the 1700's. The cemetery is in a pitiable condition. There are three graves are outside the confines of the cemetery and are in danger of extinction (these graves belong to Reuben Naogaokar Moshe Birwadkar and Miriyam Bhastekar). These graves as explained to the author are located on the grounds which comes under the ownership of the Indian Railway.
Many of the dead served in the British army and Pen was a base for the British.

The author asked the local Hazan if people come to the synagogue at Pen to conduct thanks giving services (Malida) to the prophet Elijah. The reply he received was that people normally go to the Panvel synagogue as they believe it answer their prayers.
The author comments that G-d dwells in all the synagogues and the purity of every prayer house is equal in the eyes of the Lord.

name: Poynad
desc_parts: Cemetery

The new cemetery here contains 8 graves. All dated from the 1900s. They are in an open field and most are damaged by natural forces (heavy rains and shifting of the ground). One grave is located at the Reghe Company compound. It is well protected. It is of the late Satkielji (Sakoji) Binyamin (Bapuji) Gadapkar of 1860.
There is also a synagogue in Poynad but it is no longer functioning.

name: Pune Cemetery
desc_parts: This cemetery contains graves of both Bagdadi Jews (on the left hand side) and Bene Israel (on the right hand side). In addition there are also graves of Jews from Russia

Hutment began to rise next to the enterance of the cemetery and the area became filthy. It became very difficult to carry the dead into the cemetery. The community decided to block that enterance and created a new one where it is today. Today the cemetery is guarded and also well maintained.

Mr. David Solomon is a caretaker at the Ohel David Synagogue and he also oversees the cemetery. The author was told that the municipality plans to widen the road. This will require the cemetery wall to be pushed in 5 meters putting some of the graves at the risk of being lost.

Not too far from this area another cemetery can be found. This one is harder to find but it is behind the Liberty Cinema on Parade Ground Road. During constuction of a pipeline most of the cemetery was destroyed. There are only 7 graves left here in one corner. The author identified one grave from 1812 and the other from 1852.

name: Rajkot Cemetery
desc_parts: A wall around Rajkot cemetery was built by the initiative of a single Bene Israel Songavkar girl.

name: Revdanda-Palav Crossing
desc_parts: On the way from Cheul to Alibag there's a piece of land that is used as a warehouse for logs. A Bene Israel cemetery used to stand in this place. The cemetery is now destroyed and only couple of graves were found by the author hidden under wooden logs. Since the author's visit he was told that this area was recovered and a fence was built around these graves.
The identified grave is of Binyamin Silemanji Divekar passed away on January 6 1878 at age of 30.

name: Roha Cemetery
desc_parts: There are only five graves in this Malyankar family cemetery. At the time of writing all the graves were intact. But the author notes that there's no fence or any barrier to protect this site. The earth around this area is dug by builders to make bricks.

name: Surendranagar Cemetery
desc_parts: A wall was built around this cemetery from funds collected by Mr. Aaron Dighorkar. These funds also help fix several graves at this site. There is a watchman who looks after these premises and his residence is within the cemetery compound.
There are about 30 graves at this cemetery. The oldest grave here dates back to 1806.

name: Thana Cemetery
desc_parts: There are about 200 graves here.

name: Vadodara Cemetery
desc_parts: Vadodara Cemetery is 150 years old. Its 40 odd graves are completely neglected.

name: Worli Jewish Cemetery
desc_parts: A 500 strong cemetery. Opened in 1927. A large plot of the 10 000 square yards cemetery is now occupied by a skyscraper after some graves were destroyed.

The author added that at the time of writing the serial burial number stands at 6416. This is most likely not the number of graves but rather the number used to register the graves. In reality there probably were less than 1 500 graves in existance at the Worli cemetery.
Below is a photo of the skyscraper raised on former cemetery land.
My own maternal grandparents are buried here.
